review_note: Reviewed K052S01 and SRC007. The Wechsler and Wells review directly describes cigarette smoke as an inflammatory trigger and explains that smoking-associated oxidative stress and epithelial inflammatory signaling recruit neutrophils and other immune cells. This supports Chronic cigarette smoke exposure → Airway inflammation as a contributory causal relationship. SRC007 establishes smoking-related respiratory injury and inflammatory features of COPD but does not independently verify the exact intermediate mechanism; therefore it is excluded from supporting_source_ids. Not every smoker develops the same inflammatory response or COPD. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.

review_note: Reviewed K052S02. The Wechsler and Wells review explains that inflammatory mediators and recruited immune cells contribute to mucus hypersecretion, small-airway fibrosis and structural remodeling. These changes contribute to increased airway resistance and persistent airflow obstruction in COPD. This directly supports Airway inflammation → Persistent airflow limitation in COPD as a contributory causal relationship. Other mechanisms, including alveolar destruction and reduced elastic recoil, also contribute. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.
